findings.title: Candidate hash omits project document bodies and order
findings.contract: FINISH-00-R2 requires the deterministic candidate hash to bind projects and preserve document-array order; changed bodies/order must change the hash.
findings.reproduction: The audit-only probe supplies two different project bodies with reversed section order and the same projectId/draftRevision vector. computeReviewHash ignores candidateProjects and produces the same hash.
findings.impact: A changed durable body with an unchanged revision vector is outside the review identity. Normal save code increments revisions, so this does not establish a stale-review bypass through the current save route; it remains a required hash-integrity defect.

findings.title: Private media bytes are fully materialized before the size limit and without a deadline
findings.contract: PLAT-R2-01 requires bounded private Storage reads, bounded byte accumulation, read-time limits and abort on failures.
findings.reproduction: A mocked approved row returns 5 MiB + 1 byte; readReviewedMedia calls arrayBuffer once and materializes the entire payload before validateUpload rejects the size.
findings.impact: An unexpectedly large object can consume memory proportional to its full size in owner-triggered review/save/publish/proxy paths; Storage latency is not bounded by this helper.

findings.title: PrivateDraftReviewSchema does not validate DraftRecord or cross-field review semantics
findings.contract: A1 requires exact strict ReviewIdentity and PrivateDraftReview DTO schemas and rejection of malformed fields.
findings.reproduction: The audit-only probe passes duplicate project IDs, a non-DraftRecord object in drafts, a non-timestamp string, empty checks, and canPublish=true. ReviewIdentitySchema does reject an unsafe integer through z.number().int(); this was verified and is not reported as a defect.
findings.impact: The preview route's output parse cannot guarantee the documented DTO shape or consistency. The publish service recomputes and compares ReviewIdentity, and no publish authorization bypass was reproduced.

findings.title: Maker return omits the required standalone complete requirement matrix
findings.contract: The R4 production prompt requires a complete requirement matrix as a reviewable delivery artifact.
findings.reproduction: The R4 output manifest verifies 127 delivered files and contains no requirement-matrix.json. The narrative report's compact summary table does not map every requirement to evidence and scope.
findings.impact: The reviewer had to create this audit matrix; this does not retroactively satisfy the maker's missing delivery artifact.

findings.title: Approved image selection and visual preview were not exercised in Chromium
findings.contract: A1 requires approved image selection and preview in the actual authoring workflow.
findings.reproduction: The browser test asserts the empty picker, edits alt/caption, receives the expected 422, deletes the image block, then saves. No approved image is selected or rendered in the browser.
findings.impact: The editor has an accessible selector and separate private-preview route, but the required end-to-end media flow remains unverified. No provider-backed approved asset was available.

notes: Current R4 manifest, exact patch, path set, and replacement mapping were independently reverified.
Process snapshots found no matching live process but cannot identify an exited writer; no attribution or intent is inferred.
R3 baseline and later inventory differ by 17 baseline files and include a new candidate/node_modules tree. The receipts do not attribute these changes or establish exact preservation.
Late fixture and out-of-root browser artifacts have preservation/discrepancy receipts; those records do not establish their historical writer.

limits: PGlite, synthetic auth, mocked Storage, and local browser fixtures are not native provider evidence.
Native PostgreSQL/Auth/Storage, multi-process races, provider-approved image selection, complete 503/outage matrix, CDN, deployment, PDF approval, device, recovery, and G7 were not run.
No GPT Plus #2 or other external review is claimed; Parent acceptance remains pending.
